   458	# linter-sweep
   459	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   460	#
   461	# Ports housekeeping.yml:310-382: `lake exe cache get` then
   462	# `lake build -q --log-level=info`, teed to a log, summarized by
   463	# scripts/lean_linter_warning_report.py.  The upstream job explicitly did not
   464	# open a PR (housekeeping.yml:340-341) and neither does this one; any autofix
   465	# stays a separate, human-invoked command.
   466	#
   467	# The build takes the machine-wide advisory build lock required by
   468	# DESIGN.md:81-82 — one full `lake build` at a time — so a sweep cannot race an
   469	# agent's build or the cache warmer.
   470	
   471	job_linter_sweep() {
   472	  local reporter="${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/lean_linter_warning_report.py"
   473	  require_file "${reporter}" "the linter-warning parser ports unchanged"
   474	  command -v lake >/dev/null 2>&1 || die \
   475	    "lake is not on PATH; the linter sweep is a full Lean build and cannot run without it"
   476	
   477	  mkdir -p "${REPORT_DIR}" "${LOG_DIR}"
   478	  local log_file="${LOG_DIR}/lean-build-$(timestamp).log"
   479	
   480	  note "linter-sweep: full lake build under the machine-wide build lock (this is slow)"
   481	  # THE machine-wide full-build mutex — same path and mkdir protocol as
   482	  # cache-warmer.sh, warm-worktree.sh and ci.sh (DESIGN.md invariant 7).
   483	  # A live owner is never broken; a dead owner's lock is.
   484	  local build_lock="${MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK:-${CACHE_ROOT}/.full-build-lock}"
   485	  local waited=0 wait_max="${MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S:-14400}"
   486	  while ! mkdir "${build_lock}" 2>/dev/null; do
   487	    local owner_pid
   488	    owner_pid="$(head -n 1 "${build_lock}/owner" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   489	    if [ -n "${owner_pid}" ] && kill -0 "${owner_pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
   490	      [ "${waited}" -ge "${wait_max}" ] && die \
   491	        "could not take ${build_lock} within ${wait_max}s (held by pid ${owner_pid})"
   492	      [ "${waited}" -eq 0 ] && note "waiting for build lock ${build_lock} (pid ${owner_pid})"
   493	      sleep 15; waited=$((waited + 15))
   494	    else
   495	      note "breaking stale build lock ${build_lock} (owner dead or unreadable)"
   496	      rm -rf "${build_lock}"
   497	    fi
   498	  done
   499	  printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$$" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "housekeeping linter-sweep" \
   500	    > "${build_lock}/owner"
   501	  # shellcheck disable=SC2064  # expand build_lock now, not at trap time
   502	  trap "rm -rf '${build_lock}'" RETURN
   503	  run_locked "${LOCK_DIR}/lake-build.lock" \
   504	    "${SCRIPT_DIR}/housekeeping.sh" --internal-lean-build "${log_file}"
   505	
   506	  note "linter-sweep: summarizing warnings"
   507	  python3 "${reporter}" \
   508	    --log "${log_file}" \
   509	    --json "${REPORT_DIR}/lean-linter-warnings.json" \

     2	#
     3	# github-sync.sh — push the named refs to this repository's GitHub home,
     4	# git@github.com:Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A.git (standalone repo since the
     5	# 2026-08-31 restructure; the old subtree-into-monorepo flow is retired, see
     6	# EVOLUTION.md), then refresh the read-only record snapshot.
     7	#
     8	# Usage: local/bin/github-sync.sh [ref ...]      (default: main)
     9	#
    10	# Run after every merge to main.  Only the named refs are pushed: `git push
    11	# --all` is deliberately gone.  GitHub now holds the records — issues, PRs, the
    12	# per-SHA CI statuses and the review verdicts (local/protocols/issues-prs.md) —
    13	# and a blanket push republishes every stale local branch, including the
    14	# throwaway fix branches whose heads those records are bound to.  Push what you
    15	# mean to publish.
    16	#
    17	# Exit codes:
    18	#   0  every ref pushed (the snapshot is best-effort and never fails the run)
    19	#   1  a ref did not push after 5 attempts
    20	set -euo pipefail
    21	
    22	PROG="github-sync.sh"
    23	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
    24	_common="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)"
    25	case "$_common" in */.git) ROOT="$(dirname "$_common")" ;; esac
    26	cd "$ROOT"
    27	LOCAL_BIN="$ROOT/local/bin"
    28	
    29	REFS=("$@")
    30	[ "${#REFS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || REFS=(main)
    31	
    32	git remote get-url github >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
    33	  git remote add github git@github.com:Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A.git
    34	
    35	RC=0
    36	for ref in "${REFS[@]}"; do
    37	  git rev-parse --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$ref" >/dev/null || {
    38	    echo "$PROG: no local branch '$ref'; skipping" >&2; RC=1; continue
    39	  }
    40	  pushed=0
    41	  for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    42	    if git push github "refs/heads/$ref:refs/heads/$ref"; then
    43	      echo "$PROG: pushed $ref ($(git rev-parse --short "$ref"))"
    44	      pushed=1
    45	      break
    46	    fi
    47	    echo "$PROG: push attempt $i for '$ref' failed; retrying" >&2
    48	    sleep 15
    49	  done
    50	  [ "$pushed" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$PROG: all push attempts failed for '$ref'" >&2; RC=1; }
    51	done
    52	
    53	# Audit/recovery telemetry only — never lifecycle input (gh_common.py:390-392),
    54	# so a snapshot failure must not fail a successful push.
    55	if ! python3 "$LOCAL_BIN/gh_common.py" snapshot \
    56	      --out-dir "$ROOT/results/telemetry/github-snapshot"; then
    57	  echo "$PROG: warning: the GitHub record snapshot failed; the push above still stands" >&2
    58	fi

    60	exit "$RC"

    data = json.loads(path.read_text())

    return data

def render_text_report(reports: list[IssueReport], only_flagged: bool) -> str:
    total = len(reports)
    flagged = [r for r in reports if r.is_flagged]
    scanned = [r for r in reports if r.file_citations or r.decl_citations]
    lines = [
        "Stale-issue audit report",
        "========================",
        f"issues scanned        : {total}",
        f"issues with citations : {len(scanned)}",
        f"issues flagged stale  : {len(flagged)}",
        "triage note           : keep mathematical source citations precise",
        "                       (paper/blueprint path, line, label, and",
        "                       short quotation or precise paraphrase)",
        "",
    ]
    show = flagged if only_flagged else reports
    for r in show:
        header = f"#{r.number} — {r.title}"
        lines.append(header)
        lines.append("-" * len(header))
        if r.url:
            lines.append(f"  {r.url}")
        if not r.is_flagged:
            lines.append("  (no stale citations detected)")

    14	
    15	## 1. What it is
    16	
    17	The parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull

    19	dispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one
    20	invocation, one manifest, one exit code.
    21	
    22	```
    23	local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]
    24	                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]

    27	`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the

    40	
    41	| Precondition | Why it is fatal |
    42	|---|---|

    44	| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |

    50	and `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely
    51	stops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green

   183	## 5. Publication
   184	
   185	Evidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against

+  if [ "$CONCLUSION" = success ]; then
+    post_status "$HEAD_SHA" local-ci/summary success "all gating steps passed (${RUN_SECONDS}s)"
+  else
+    post_status "$HEAD_SHA" local-ci/summary failure "conclusion=$CONCLUSION (${RUN_SECONDS}s); see the manifest comment"
+  fi

+fi
+

item.text: The tests expose a second structural gap: changes to most of the newly added workflow engine do not set CI’s `workflow` path flag, so the workflow’s own unit tests can be skipped while every required context is reported successful. I’m checking whether any broader gate compensates for that before treating it as a merge blocker.

    77	
    78	`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
    79	never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
    80	`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
    81	commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
    82	that refuse by default:
    83	
    84	1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely
    85	   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;
    86	2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip
    87	   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here;
    88	3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on
    89	   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state
    90	   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
    91	4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or
    92	   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is
    93	   `success` there;
    94	5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The one GitHub layer for ``local/bin`` — a thin, fail-closed wrapper over ``gh``.

GitHub is the single source of truth for issues, PRs, CI evidence (commit
statuses on the exact head SHA), review verdicts (COMMENT reviews bound to a
commit id), and merges (REST merge guarded by an exact-SHA match).  This module
is the only place workflow scripts talk to GitHub, as a Python import or via
its CLI (``gh_common.py <subcommand> ...``) from shell.

Design rules (local/protocols/issues-prs.md):

* At most one write mutation per invocation of a helper; ambiguity after a
  failed write is resolved by re-reading state and adopting, never by
  repeating the mutation.  Writes that are idempotent by content (statuses,
  close-PATCH) may be retried blindly.
* Everything uses ``gh api`` (raw REST), so no feature of a modern ``gh`` CLI
  is required — the exact-SHA merge guard is the REST ``sha`` parameter, not a
  CLI flag.
* Fail closed: a network failure after retries raises; no local fallback
  record is ever written.

Environment: ``MIPSTARRE_GH`` (gh binary; default ``gh`` on PATH, then
``~/.local/bin/gh``), ``MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO`` (``owner/repo``; default
parsed from the ``github`` remote of the primary checkout).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

)

_REMOTE_RE = re.compile(r"github\.com[:/]([^/]+/[^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?$")


def gh_bin() -> str:
    override = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_GH")
    if override:
        return override
    found = shutil.which("gh")
    if found:
        return found
    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "bin" / "gh"
    if fallback.exists():
        return str(fallback)
    raise LayerError("gh CLI not found (set MIPSTARRE_GH or install gh)")


def repo_slug(repo_root: Path | None = None) -> str:
    override = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO")
    if override:
        return override
    root = repo_root or default_repo_root()
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "remote", "get-url", "github"],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    if proc.returncode == 0:
        match = _REMOTE_RE.search(proc.stdout.strip())
        if match:
            return match.group(1)
    raise LayerError(
        "cannot resolve the GitHub repo: set MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO=owner/repo "
        "or add a 'github' remote to the primary checkout"
    )


def run_gh(args: list[str], *, input_text: str | None = None,
           mutation: bool = False, idempotent: bool = False,
           retries: int = 3) -> str:
    """Run ``gh`` and return stdout; raise ``LayerError`` on final failure.

    A non-idempotent mutation is attempted exactly once — the caller owns
    ambiguity recovery by re-reading state.  Reads and idempotent mutations
    retry on transient failures with linear backoff.
    """
    attempts = 1 if (mutation and not idempotent) else max(1, retries)
    env = dict(os.environ, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED="1", GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER="1",
               NO_COLOR="1", GH_PAGER="cat")
    last_err = ""
    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [gh_bin(), *args], input=input_text,
            capture_output=True, text=True, env=env,
        )
        if proc.returncode == 0:
            return proc.stdout
        last_err = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout or "").strip()
        if attempt < attempts and _TRANSIENT_RE.search(last_err):
            time.sleep(5 * attempt)
            continue
        break
    raise LayerError(f"gh {' '.join(args[:3])}... failed: {last_err[:2000]}")


def api(path: str, *, method: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None,
        paginate: bool = False, mutation: bool = False,
        idempotent: bool = False, absolute: bool = False):
    """Call the REST API under ``repos/<slug>/`` (or an absolute *path*).

    Pagination is manual (``?per_page=100&page=N``) so nothing here depends on
    a modern ``gh``.  Returns parsed JSON (``None`` for an empty response).
    """
    full = path if absolute else f"repos/{repo_slug()}/{path}"

    def one(page_path: str):
        args = ["api", page_path]
        if method:
            args += ["-X", method]
        input_text = None
        if payload is not None:
            args += ["--input", "-"]
            input_text = json.dumps(payload)
        out = run_gh(args, input_text=input_text, mutation=mutation,
                     idempotent=idempotent)
        return json.loads(out) if out.strip() else None

    if not paginate:
        return one(full)

    sep = "&" if "?" in full else "?"
    rows: list = []
    page = 1
    while True:
        batch = one(f"{full}{sep}per_page={PAGE}&page={page}")
        if not batch:
            break
        rows.extend(batch)
        if len(batch) < PAGE:
            break
        page += 1
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Commit statuses — CI and review evidence, bound to the exact head SHA
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def post_status(sha: str, context: str, state: str, description: str = "",
                target_url: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Post one commit status.  Idempotent by content: latest-per-context wins."""
    if state not in ("pending", "success", "failure", "error"):
        raise LayerError(f"invalid status state {state!r}")
    payload = {"state": state, "context": context,
               "description": description[:140]}
    if target_url:
        payload["target_url"] = target_url
    api(f"statuses/{sha}", method="POST", payload=payload,
        mutation=True, idempotent=True)


def latest_statuses(sha: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Latest status per context on *sha* (rows arrive newest-first)."""
    rows = api(f"commits/{sha}/statuses", paginate=True)
    latest: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for row in rows:
        context = row.get("context") or ""
        if context and context not in latest:
            latest[context] = {"state": row.get("state"),
                               "description": row.get("description") or "",
                               "created_at": row.get("created_at") or ""}
    return latest


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pull requests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def pr_view(number: int) -> dict:
    return api(f"pulls/{number}")


def pr_for_branch(branch: str) -> dict | None:
    """The unique open PR whose head is *branch*, or None."""
    owner = repo_slug().split("/")[0]
    rows = api(f"pulls?state=open&head={owner}:{branch}", paginate=True)
    if len(rows) > 1:
        raise LayerError(f"multiple open PRs for head {branch!r}")
    return rows[0] if rows else None


def ensure_pr_comment(number: int, marker: str, body: str) -> int:
    """Create or update the single PR comment carrying *marker*.

    The marker (an HTML comment) is the idempotency key: an existing comment
    is PATCHed in place; after an ambiguous POST failure the list is re-read
    and an adopted comment is not re-posted.
    """
    full = _marked_body(marker, body)
    existing = _find_comment(number, marker)
    if existing is not None:
        api(f"issues/comments/{existing}", method="PATCH",
            payload={"body": full}, mutation=True, idempotent=True)
        return existing
    try:
        created = api(f"issues/{number}/comments", method="POST",
                      payload={"body": full}, mutation=True)
        return int(created["id"])
    except LayerError:
        adopted = _find_comment(number, marker)
        if adopted is not None:
            return adopted
        raise


def _find_comment(number: int, marker: str) -> int | None:
    for row in api(f"issues/{number}/comments", paginate=True):
        if marker in (row.get("body") or ""):
            return int(row["id"])
    return None


def _marked_body(marker: str, body: str) -> str:
    if len(body) > COMMENT_BODY_LIMIT:
        body = body[:COMMENT_BODY_LIMIT] + "\n\n*(truncated; the full text is in runtime storage / telemetry)*"
    return f"{marker}\n{body}"


def post_review(number: int, commit_id: str, marker: str, body: str) -> str:
    """Post one COMMENT review bound to *commit_id*; marker-idempotent.

    Single-account repos cannot self-APPROVE, so every local verdict is a
    COMMENT review; adverseness travels in the ``local-review/summary`` status,
    not in a review state.  Returns ``"exists"`` or the new review id.
    """
    for row in api(f"pulls/{number}/reviews", paginate=True):
        if row.get("commit_id") == commit_id and marker in (row.get("body") or ""):
            return "exists"
    payload = {"commit_id": commit_id, "event": "COMMENT",
               "body": _marked_body(marker, body)}
    try:
        created = api(f"pulls/{number}/reviews", method="POST",
                      payload=payload, mutation=True)
        return str(created.get("id"))
    except LayerError:
        for row in api(f"pulls/{number}/reviews", paginate=True):
            if row.get("commit_id") == commit_id and marker in (row.get("body") or ""):
                return "adopted"
        raise


def pr_reviews(number: int) -> list[dict]:
    return api(f"pulls/{number}/reviews", paginate=True)


def merge_pr(number: int, sha: str) -> str:
    """Merge PR *number* iff its head is exactly *sha*; verify topology.

    The REST ``sha`` parameter makes GitHub reject the merge when the head
    moved — the atomic exact-head guard, independent of the gh CLI version.
    Returns the merge commit SHA after verifying it has exactly two parents
    with the frozen head second.
    """
    put_error = ""
    try:
        api(f"pulls/{number}/merge", method="PUT",
            payload={"sha": sha, "merge_method": "merge"}, mutation=True)
    except LayerError as exc:
        put_error = str(exc)  # fall through: the read-back below is the authority
    pr = pr_view(number)
    if not pr.get("merged"):
        state = pr.get("state")
        head = (pr.get("head") or {}).get("sha")
        detail = f"; merge call said: {put_error[:400]}" if put_error else ""
        raise LayerError(
            f"PR #{number} did not merge (state={state}, head={head}, "
            f"expected {sha}){detail}")
    merge_commit = pr.get("merge_commit_sha") or ""
    commit = api(f"commits/{merge_commit}")
    parents = [p.get("sha") for p in commit.get("parents") or []]
    if len(parents) != 2 or parents[1] != sha:
        raise LayerError(
            f"PR #{number} merge commit {merge_commit} has parents {parents}; "
            f"expected two with head {sha} second — someone else merged?")
    return merge_commit


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Issues
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def list_labels() -> list[str]:
    return [row["name"] for row in api("labels", paginate=True)]


def issue_view(number: int) -> dict:
    return api(f"issues/{number}")


def issue_create(title: str, body: str, labels: tuple[str, ...] = (),
                 parent: int | None = None, key: str | None = None) -> int:
    """Create an issue; validate labels; optionally link as a sub-issue.

    With *key*, a ``<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: ... -->`` marker is embedded and
    an ambiguous create failure adopts the existing issue instead of
    duplicating it.
    """
    check_bracket_free(title, "issue title")
    if labels:
        known = set(list_labels())
        missing = sorted(set(labels) - known)
        if missing:
            raise LayerError(
                f"labels not in the repository: {missing} — create them on "
                f"GitHub first (gh label create) or drop them")
    marker = f"<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: {key} -->" if key else None
    full_body = f"{marker}\n{body}" if marker else body
    # Adoption never returns early: the parent link below must run even when the
    # issue already exists (a prior run may have died between create and link).
    number = _find_issue_by_marker(marker) if marker else None
    if number is None:
        payload: dict = {"title": title, "body": full_body}
        if labels:
            payload["labels"] = list(labels)
        try:
            created = api("issues", method="POST", payload=payload, mutation=True)
            number = int(created["number"])
        except LayerError:
            if marker:
                number = _find_issue_by_marker(marker)
            if number is None:
                raise
    if parent is not None:
        add_sub_issue(parent, number)
    return number


def _find_issue_by_marker(marker: str) -> int | None:
    rows = api(f"issues?state=all&per_page={PAGE}&sort=created&direction=desc")
    for row in rows or []:
        if "pull_request" in row:
            continue
        if marker in (row.get("body") or ""):
            return int(row["number"])
    return None


def add_sub_issue(parent: int, child: int) -> None:
    child_id = issue_view(child)["id"]
    try:
        api(f"issues/{parent}/sub_issues", method="POST",
            payload={"sub_issue_id": child_id}, mutation=True)
    except LayerError as exc:
        # Re-linking an existing child is a 422; adopt it.
        for row in api(f"issues/{parent}/sub_issues", paginate=True):
            if int(row.get("number", -1)) == child:
                return
        raise exc


def open_sub_issues(number: int) -> list[int]:
    rows = api(f"issues/{number}/sub_issues", paginate=True)
    return [int(r["number"]) for r in rows if r.get("state") == "open"]


def issue_close(number: int, reason: str = "completed",
                comment: str | None = None) -> None:
    if reason not in ("completed", "not-planned"):
        raise LayerError(f"invalid close reason {reason!r}")
    if comment:
        ensure_pr_comment(number, f"<!-- mipstarre-close-note-{number} -->", comment)
    api(f"issues/{number}", method="PATCH",
        payload={"state": "closed",
                 "state_reason": "not_planned" if reason == "not-planned" else reason},
        mutation=True, idempotent=True)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read-only snapshot (audit/recovery telemetry — never lifecycle input)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def snapshot(out_dir: Path) -> None:
    issues = [r for r in api("issues?state=open", paginate=True)
              if "pull_request" not in r]
    pulls = api("pulls?state=open", paginate=True)
    meta = {"generated": utcnow(), "repo": repo_slug(),
            "open_issues": len(issues), "open_pulls": len(pulls)}
    out = Path(out_dir)
    atomic_write(out / "open-issues.json", json.dumps(issues, indent=1) + "\n")
    atomic_write(out / "open-pulls.json", json.dumps(pulls, indent=1) + "\n")
    atomic_write(out / "metadata.json", json.dumps(meta, indent=1) + "\n")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI — the shell scripts' entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _emit(value) -> None:
    if value is None:
        return
    if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
        json.dump(value, sys.stdout, indent=1)
        sys.stdout.write("\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(f"{value}\n")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("pr-view"); p.add_argument("number", type=int)
    p = sub.add_parser("pr-for-branch"); p.add_argument("branch")
    p = sub.add_parser("post-status")
    p.add_argument("sha"); p.add_argument("context"); p.add_argument("state")
    p.add_argument("--desc", default=""); p.add_argument("--target-url")
    p = sub.add_parser("latest-statuses"); p.add_argument("sha")
    p = sub.add_parser("ensure-pr-comment")
    p.add_argument("number", type=int); p.add_argument("marker")
    p.add_argument("--body-file", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("post-review")
    p.add_argument("number", type=int); p.add_argument("commit_id")
    p.add_argument("marker"); p.add_argument("--body-file", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("pr-reviews"); p.add_argument("number", type=int)
    p = sub.add_parser("merge-pr")
    p.add_argument("number", type=int); p.add_argument("sha")
    p = sub.add_parser("issue-view"); p.add_argument("number", type=int)
    p = sub.add_parser("issue-create")
    p.add_argument("--title", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--body-file", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--label", action="append", default=[])
    p.add_argument("--parent", type=int)
    p.add_argument("--key")
    p = sub.add_parser("issue-close")
    p.add_argument("number", type=int)
    p.add_argument("--reason", default="completed")
    p.add_argument("--comment")
    p = sub.add_parser("open-sub-issues"); p.add_argument("number", type=int)
    p = sub.add_parser("list-labels")
    p = sub.add_parser("snapshot"); p.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("repo-slug")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        if args.cmd == "pr-view":
            _emit(pr_view(args.number))
        elif args.cmd == "pr-for-branch":
            _emit(pr_for_branch(args.branch))
        elif args.cmd == "post-status":
            post_status(args.sha, args.context, args.state,
                        description=args.desc, target_url=args.target_url)
        elif args.cmd == "latest-statuses":
            _emit(latest_statuses(args.sha))
        elif args.cmd == "ensure-pr-comment":
            _emit(ensure_pr_comment(args.number, args.marker,
                                    Path(args.body_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
        elif args.cmd == "post-review":
            _emit(post_review(args.number, args.commit_id, args.marker,
                              Path(args.body_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
        elif args.cmd == "pr-reviews":
            _emit(pr_reviews(args.number))
        elif args.cmd == "merge-pr":
            _emit(merge_pr(args.number, args.sha))
        elif args.cmd == "issue-view":
            _emit(issue_view(args.number))
        elif args.cmd == "issue-create":
            _emit(issue_create(args.title,
                               Path(args.body_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                               labels=tuple(args.label), parent=args.parent,
                               key=args.key))
        elif args.cmd == "issue-close":
            issue_close(args.number, reason=args.reason, comment=args.comment)
        elif args.cmd == "open-sub-issues":
            _emit(open_sub_issues(args.number))
        elif args.cmd == "list-labels":
            _emit(list_labels())
        elif args.cmd == "snapshot":
            snapshot(Path(args.out_dir))
        elif args.cmd == "repo-slug":
            _emit(repo_slug())
    except LayerError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: {exc}\n")
        return 2
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

   245	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   246	
   247	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis
   248	
   249	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
   250	|---|---|---|
   251	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   252	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   253	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   261	
   262	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   263	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or explicitly overridden by the user — and per
   268	`docs/pr_review_management.md`, "never merge without user consent" is the
   269	standing rule that override is *not* the automation's to exercise.
   270	
   271	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   272	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   273	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   274	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   275	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   276	
   277	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   278	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   279	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
   280	merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
   281	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   282	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

   415	#: A path segment into the archived registries.  The REST API also speaks
   416	#: ``issues/...``, so the two are told apart by what follows: a route always
   417	#: continues with an f-string field (``issues/{number}/comments``) or with
   418	#: ``comments/{id}`` (gh_common.py:213), while a tree reference continues with a
   419	#: literal id, glob or filename.
   420	_TREE_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.-])(?:issues|prs)/")
   421	_REST_ROUTE_RE = re.compile(r"^issues/(?:\{|comments/\{)")
   422	
   423	#: The other shape a tree reference takes: a join onto the repository root.
   424	_TREE_JOIN_RE = re.compile(
   425	    r"""(?:\$\{?ROOT\}?|\$\{?REPO_ROOT\}?|repo_root|REPO_ROOT)\s*/\s*["']?(?:issues|prs)\b""")

   428	def _active_source(path: Path) -> str:
   429	    """The file's live code: comments and docstrings blanked, line numbers kept.
   430	
   431	    Every surviving mention of the registries is historical narration ("Pre-0007
   432	    this wrote ``prs/<id>-<slug>/pr.md``", issue_new.py:2-5), so a grep over raw
   433	    text cannot express the rule.  Python comments come from ``tokenize`` (a
   434	    ``#`` inside a string is not a comment token) and docstrings from ``ast``;
   435	    shell keeps only its non-comment lines.
   436	    """
   437	    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   438	    if path.suffix == ".sh":
   439	        return "\n".join("" if line.lstrip().startswith("#") else line
   440	                         for line in text.splitlines())

item.text: Three merge-gate defects are now independently confirmed: dirty worktrees can mint evidence for uncommitted bytes, adjudication can bypass review without satisfying its documented round/disposition requirements, and GitHub closing syntax can evade the sub-issue dependency check. I’m narrowing the final ledger to defects that change safety or correctness, rather than listing every protocol mismatch.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"
GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS="$(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)"

run_without_git_local_env() (
  # Git exports repository-local variables while running hooks.  Several script
  # tests create temporary repositories; keep those tests independent of this
  # checkout.
  unset $GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS
  "$@"
)

STAGED_FILES="$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR)"
if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
  exit 0

# workflow scaffolding is budgeted at <=400 changed lines per commit.  This is
# mechanical enforcement — repeated verbal correction of scaffolding bloat did
# not stick, so the budget lives in the hook.  The override env var is granted
# by the OWNER per commit, never self-granted by an agent session.
INFRA_CHANGED="$(git diff --cached --numstat -- local/ .githooks/ scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py \
  | awk '{added=$1; deleted=$2; if (added != "-") total+=added+deleted} END {print total+0}')"

   wrong core statement, source drift on a paper-labelled theorem, an A1–A6
   anti-pattern, or a proof-integrity blocker.
 - **S4 Critical** — an unjustified key assumption, a missing essential step, an
   undefined critical quantity, a stale or invalid `\leanok`.
 - **S3 Major** — an incomplete supporting lemma, an approximation with no error
   bound, a missing boundary condition, no docstring on a new public declaration.
 - **S2 Minor** — naming or notation drift, a missing intermediate step, import
   churn: fix it, but validity is unaffected.
 - **S1 Cosmetic** — typo, formatting, slightly imprecise phrasing.
 - **S0 Verified** — a passing check, recorded so the next pass need not redo it.

 5 is certain, 3 field-dependent, 1 speculative; when unsure lower the confidence,
 not the severity.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shared non-registry helpers for ``local/bin``.

Extracted verbatim from ``track.py`` when the local issue/PR registry was
retired in favor of GitHub-native records (issue 0007; the registry itself is
archived read-only under ``results/telemetry/registry-archive/``).  Only the
pieces with no registry coupling live here: runtime locations, untrusted-text
sanitization, naming rules, the per-entity advisory lock, and the atomic
writer.  Nothing outside ``local/`` may import this module.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import errno
import fcntl
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Locations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: Runtime state (locks, caches) never lives in the repository — DESIGN.md:37.
CACHE_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT", "~/.cache/mipstarre-dev"))

#: Characters banned from titles.  docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124 names exactly
#: this pair: bracketed prefixes leak into bot-generated branch names and ``]``
#: breaks part of the PR automation stack.  A title may still contain ``:``
#: ("Tracking: ..." is the documented idiom).
FORBIDDEN_TITLE_CHARS = "[]"

#: Characters banned from branch names: the pair above plus the git refname
#: metacharacters, which ``git check-ref-format`` rejects for the same
#: structural reason — a name that travels through shell, path and regex
#: contexts must survive all three.
FORBIDDEN_REF_CHARS = "[]~^:?*\\ \t"


def default_repo_root() -> Path:
    """Repository root, assuming this file stays at ``local/bin/wf_util.py``."""
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def cache_root() -> Path:
    return CACHE_ROOT.expanduser()


def lock_dir() -> Path:
    return cache_root() / "locks"


def utcnow() -> str:
    """Timestamp format used across telemetry and generated records."""
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")


class LayerError(RuntimeError):
    """Operator-facing failure: printed without a traceback by ``main``."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Untrusted-text sanitization
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_CONTROL_RE = re.compile(r"[\u0000-\u0008\u000B\u000C\u000E-\u001F\u007F]")

#: Truncation limits copied from the parent's sanitize step
#: (issue-automation.yml:124-128): title 200, body 5000.
TITLE_LIMIT = 200
BODY_LIMIT = 5000


def sanitize(text: str | None, limit: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Strip control characters, break ``` fences, optionally truncate.

    Verbatim port of the ``Sanitize issue content`` step at
    ``.github/workflows/issue-automation.yml:122-128``.  Issue and PR text is
    untrusted even when it originates locally — and doubly so now that bodies
    round-trip through GitHub, where anyone with repo read access can quote
    them.  Fence-breaking inserts zero-width spaces so a body cannot close a
    fenced block that frames it as data.
    """
    cleaned = _CONTROL_RE.sub("", text or "")
    cleaned = cleaned.replace("```", "\u200b`\u200b`\u200b`")
    if limit is not None:
        cleaned = cleaned[:limit]
    return cleaned


def check_bracket_free(value: str, what: str, chars: str = FORBIDDEN_TITLE_CHARS) -> None:
    """Raise when *value* carries a character that breaks name propagation.

    docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124: "Avoid prefixes like ``[Chapter 9] ...``:
    bot-generated branch names inherit those characters, and ``]`` breaks part
    of the PR automation stack."  Slugs and branch names derive from titles
    mechanically, so the rule is enforced at the point of creation.
    """
    bad = sorted({c for c in value if c in chars})
    if bad:
        rendered = " ".join(repr(c) for c in bad)
        raise LayerError(
            f"{what} contains reserved character(s) {rendered}: {value!r}\n"
            "Bracketed prefixes leak into branch names and break name-derived "
            "automation (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). Rewrite the text, e.g. "
            "'Chapter 9 - finish the sandwich-chain corollaries'."
        )


def slugify(title: str, max_words: int = 8) -> str:
    """Lowercase, hyphenated, bracket-free slug derived from a title."""
    lowered = title.lower()
    words = [w for w in re.split(r"[^a-z0-9]+", lowered) if w]
    if not words:
        raise LayerError(f"title {title!r} yields an empty slug; use words a-z0-9")
    slug = "-".join(words[:max_words])[:60].strip("-")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*", slug):
        raise LayerError(f"derived slug {slug!r} is not bracket-free lowercase-kebab")
    return slug


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Advisory locking
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_HELD: dict[str, int] = {}


@contextmanager
def file_lock(name: str, *, timeout_note: str | None = None) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Exclusive advisory lock under ``~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/<name>``.

    The hazard is two agent sessions mutating the same runtime state; a
    per-entity ``flock`` plus the atomic writer below covers it.  Re-entrant
    within one process so a caller may hold a lock while a helper re-acquires
    it.
    """
    if _HELD.get(name):
        _HELD[name] += 1
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            _HELD[name] -= 1
        return

    directory = lock_dir()
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = directory / f"{name}.lock"
    fd = os.open(str(path), os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o644)
    try:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except OSError as exc:
            if exc.errno not in (errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES):
                raise
            sys.stderr.write(f"waiting for lock {path} ...\n")
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        os.ftruncate(fd, 0)
        os.write(fd, f"{os.getpid()}\n".encode())
        _HELD[name] = 1
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            _HELD.pop(name, None)
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Atomic writes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    """Write *text* to *path* via tempfile + ``os.replace``.

    Used for runtime artifacts and telemetry snapshots: a half-written file
    must never be observable.
    """
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(path.parent), prefix=f".{path.name}.", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(text)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise
    dir_fd = os.open(str(path.parent), os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)

def create_pr(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    repo_root = args.repo_root.resolve()
    issue_id = track.normalize_id(args.issue)
    issue = track.load_issue(repo_root, issue_id)
    if issue.state != "open":
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"warning: issue #{issue_id} is {issue.state}; opening a PR against a "
            "closed issue is unusual\n"
        )

    lint_branch(args.branch, issue_id)

    title = track.sanitize(args.title, track.TITLE_LIMIT).strip()
    if not title:
        raise LayerError("--title is empty after sanitization")
    track.check_bracket_free(title, "PR title")
    slug = track.slugify(title)

    taxonomy = track.load_taxonomy(repo_root)
    labels = sorted({name for name in issue.labels if name in taxonomy})
    for chunk in args.labels:
        for name in (part.strip() for part in chunk.split(",")):
            if not name:
                continue
            if name in taxonomy.banned:
                raise LayerError(f"label {name!r} is banned: {taxonomy.banned[name]}")
            if name not in taxonomy:
                raise LayerError(f"label {name!r} is not defined in local/labels.yml")
            if name not in labels:
                labels.append(name)
    labels = sorted(labels)

    head_sha = git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{args.branch}^{{commit}}")
    if head_sha is None:
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"warning: branch {args.branch!r} does not resolve in this repository; "
            "head_sha stays null and pr_merge.py will refuse until ci.sh records "
            "one.\n"
        )

    directory = track.prs_dir(repo_root)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with track.file_lock("prs-seq"):
        existing = [p.id for p in track.iter_prs(repo_root)]
        if args.dry_run:
            pr_id = f"{(max([int(e) for e in existing], default=0) + 1):04d}"
        else:
            pr_id = track.next_sequence_id(directory / ".seq", existing)

    record_dir = directory / f"{pr_id}-{slug}"
    path = record_dir / "pr.md"
    if path.exists():
        raise LayerError(f"{path} already exists; refusing to overwrite")

def _parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="pr_open.py",
        description=__doc__,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    parser.add_argument("--issue", required=True, metavar="ID",
                        help="issue this PR addresses")
    parser.add_argument("--branch", required=True,
                        help="branch name; must embed the issue id")
    parser.add_argument("--title", required=True,
                        help="conventional-commit title, e.g. 'feat(Quantum): ...'")
    parser.add_argument("--base", default="main", help="merge target (default: main)")
    parser.add_argument("--closes", action="store_true",
                        help="use 'Closes #N' (auto-close on merge) instead of "
                             "'Addresses #N' (keep open)")
    parser.add_argument("--labels", action="append", default=[],
                        help="extra labels beyond those copied from the issue")
    parser.add_argument("--no-auto-fix", action="store_true",
                        help="record auto_fix: false so the fix loop skips this PR")
    parser.add_argument("--repo-root", type=Path, default=track.default_repo_root(),
                        help="repository root (default: two levels above this script)")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                        help="print the record that would be written, write nothing")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = _parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    try:
        return create_pr(args)
    except LayerError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"pr_open.py: {exc}\n")
        return 2

item.text: The auto-fix concurrency path adds two more correctness failures: a superseding run can inherit an unpushed local fix while still trusting the old remote SHA’s evidence and iteration count, and the cap can be reached before that accumulated commit is pushed. Both defeat the history-based cap and exact-head review guarantees, so they need to stay in the blocking set.

Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing. These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof. These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`\npass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only\nthat one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has\nnothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written\ndisposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.\n\n**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is\nnot mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the\nunchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\\s*[-*]\\s*\\[ \\]`, applied to\nthe marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is\nclean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else\nmust be resolved, outdated, or explicitly overridden by the user — and per\n`docs/pr_review_management.md`, \"never merge without user consent\" is the\nstanding rule that override is *not* the automation's to exercise.\n\nFindings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker\n`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger\nwritten at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at\nall is \"not reviewed\", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the\nnext review re-derives from the new diff.\n\nA second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any\n`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run\ndirectory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not\nmerge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and\n# Protocol — local PR CI\n\nNormative protocol for `local/bin/ci.sh`, the local replacement for\n`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` (frozen under `.github/`, never executed here).\nRead `meta.md` first; `build-cache.md` owns the hot-main cache this protocol\nconsumes but never writes.\n\n`ci.sh <pr-number>` is the **only** thing allowed to publish the `local-ci/*`\ncommit statuses. Everything downstream — `review.sh` (invariant 2: review only\nafter green CI on the same head SHA), `autofix.sh` (invariant 3: sync/audit\nfailures are never auto-fixed), and the merge gate in `pr_merge.py` — reads\nthose exact-head statuses and the manifest comment this script publishes\n(`local/protocols/issues-prs.md` §2), and nothing else.\n\n## 1. What it is\n\nThe parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull\nrequest produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix\ndispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one\ninvocation, one manifest, one exit code.\n\n```\nlocal/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]\n                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]\n```\n\n`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the\nhead SHA from GitHub (`gh_common.py pr-view`), finds the branch's worktree (via\n`git worktree list`, falling back to `.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and\nruns everything **inside that worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary\ncheckout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the\nrun starts.\n\nExit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at\nleast one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start\n(unknown PR number, missing worktree, unresolvable base, GitHub unreachable —\na GitHub error never degrades to a local record).\n\n### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips\n\n| Precondition | Why it is fatal |\n|---|---|\n| GitHub returns an open PR with a head branch | there is no branch to test |\n| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |\n| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the \"checks silently stopped running\" failure the parent repo patched twice |\n| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |\n| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |\n\nThere is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`\nand `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely\nstops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green\nlight it never earned. If CI must not run, do not run it — the head SHA simply\nkeeps whatever statuses it already carries.\n\n## 2. Exit-code semantics are\npreserved exactly: `::warning` never failed a job, and the `^ERROR:` grep\nalways did.\n\n### Steps that did not run\n\nA step whose area did not change is recorded `skipped` with the reason — never\nomitted. A skipped step is green for the merge gate, exactly as a skipped\nGitHub job is. This is why the gating globs are load-bearing (§3): a glob that\nunder-matches turns a real gate into a permanent, invisible `skipped`.\n\n## 3. Gating globs — keep in lockstep\n\n`git diff --name-only --no-renames <merge-base> <head>` replaces\n`dorny/paths-filter@v3`. `--no-renames` is deliberate: reporting both the old\nand the new path means a rename *out of* a gated tree still trips that tree's\nfilter, and deletions count. `*` in these patterns spans `/`, matching\nminimatch's `**`.\n\n| Area | Globs | Parent |\n|---|---|---|\n| `lean` | `*.lean`, `lakefile.*`, `lean-toolchain`, `lake-manifest.json` | `pr-ci.yml:84-88` |\n| `mip_lean` | `MIPStarRE/*.lean` | `:89-90` |\n| `ldt_lean` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/*.lean` | `:91-92` |\n| `blueprint` | `blueprint/*` | `:93-94` |\n| `blueprint_src` | `blueprint/src/*` | `:95-96` |\n| `tex_chapter` | `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` | `:97-98` |\n| `paper_gaps` | `docs/paper-gaps/*`, `texra-blueprint.toml`, `MIPStarRE/*.lean`, `blueprint/src/*`, `docs/*.md` | `:99-107` |\n| `scripts` | `scripts/*` | `:108-109` |\n| `comparator` | `scripts/comparator/*` | `:110-111` |\n| `workflow` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml`, `local/bin/ci.sh`, `local/protocols/ci.md` | `:112-113`, extended |\n\n> **Lockstep warning.** These globs must move together with the trees the audit\n> scripts actually scan. The parent repo patched the `paper_gaps` filter twice\n> after checks silently never ran — the note at `pr-ci.yml:102-104` is the scar.\n> The failure mode is asymmetric: an over-broad glob costs CPU, an under-broad\n> glob costs a merged regression that no check ever looked at. When you widen\n> a scan tree in `scripts/*.py`, widen the matching glob in `ci.sh` in the same\n> commit, per `meta.md` §5.\n\nThe `workflow` area is the one deliberate extension. On GitHub it meant \"the\nworkflow file changed, so re-run everything\"; locally the CI definition lives\nin three files — the frozen reference, this driver, and this protocol — and any\nof them changing forces a full run.\n\n## 4. Manifest schema\n\nBuilt in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then\nposted as the manifest PR comment (§5):\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci/<pr>/<head_sha>.json          complete run\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci/<pr>/<head_sha>.partial.json  --only / --skip-build\n```\n\nStep logs live outside the repository, under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"schema\": 1,\n  \"generator\": \"local/bin/ci.sh\",\n  \"replaces\": \".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml\",\n  \"pr\": 7,                       // GitHub PR number\n  \"branch\": \"issue-7-qpbt-basis\",\n  \"base\": \"main\",                // from the GitHub PR\n  \"base_ref\": \"origin/main\",     // what actually resolved\n  \"merge_base\": \"<sha>\",\n  \"head_sha\": \"<sha>\",           // the SHA every step ran against\n  \"worktree\": \"/abs/path\",\n  \"started\": \"2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800\",   // ISO-8601 with offset\n  \"finished\": \"2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800\",\n  \"seconds\": 1125,               // whole run, integer\n  \"conclusion\": \"success\",       // success | failure | error\n  \"partial\": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict\n  \"areas\": { \"lean\": true, \"blueprint_src\": false, ... },\n  \"changed_files\": [\"MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean\", ...],\n  \"warnings\": [\"texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...\", ...],\n  \"steps\": [\n    {\n      \"step\": \"build\",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight\n      \"outcome\": \"success\",      // success | failure | error | skipped\n      \"seconds\": 883,\n      \"log_path\": \"/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log\",\n      \"blocking\": true,\n      \"note\": \"\"                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nOutcome vocabulary — the distinction is what routes the auto-fix loop:\n\n| `outcome` | Meaning | Auto-fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| `success` | the step ran and passed | — |\n| `failure` | the step ran and the code is wrong | `build` → ci-fix, `blueprint-render` → blueprint-fix, everything else → **never** |\n| `error` | the step could not run (missing tool, unbootstrapped worktree, build lock unavailable) | never — this is an operator problem, not a code problem |\n| `skipped` | gated out, or excluded by `--only` / `--skip-build` | — |\n\n`conclusion` is `failure` if any step failed, else `error` if any step errored,\nelse `success`. The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == \"success\"`.\n\n## 5. Publication\n\nEvidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against\n(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:\n\n* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the\n  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`\n  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish\n  \"absent\" from \"not applicable\";\n* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;\n* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked\n  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.\n\n`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,\nkilled or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the\nreview gate's \"green CI on the same head SHA\" check (invariant 2) fails closed.\nImmediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch\ntip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits\nnonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.\n\nA **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`) publishes no gate-satisfying status\nset and keeps its manifest in runtime storage only. Partial runs are a debugging\naid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and they must not\nclobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.\n\n## 6. Concurrency and locks\n\nTwo advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each\nholds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its\nowner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`\n(default 3 h).\n\n| Lock | Scope | On contention |\n|---|---|---|\n| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |\n| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |\n\nOnly the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and\ntake nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and\ntake nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them\nper-file without serializing.\n\n`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs\n(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —\nthe ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:\nkilling a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.\nSo a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is\nwaited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove\nthe lease directories by hand.\n\n## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache\n\n`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the\nshared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save\npolicy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of\n~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,\nso no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a\nworktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.\n\n1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,\n   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:\n   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a\n   hard error.\n   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);\n     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.\n2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and\n   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never\n   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main\n   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,\n   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`\n   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run\n   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.\n3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at\n   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`.
